title: sudograph spec
description: Field names are English because they are the contract. Values keep the customer's own business vocabulary.

mode.description: source_projection is phase one: declared table keys, columns and foreign keys only; checked against the source at every load. No formulas, inline facts, workflow gaps or business rules.

dimensions.description: Named axes the facts are partitioned along — reporting period, legal entity, currency. A dimension DIVIDES the rows: the 2023 rows and the 2025 rows are disjoint and the periods sum to the whole, which is why any number of them compose freely. A basis does the opposite — it is a complete reading of all the facts — so bases list rather than multiply.

bases.description: Named readings the same structure is computed under — the book figures, the restated ones, the tax ones. A flat list, not a product of dimensions: two rule axes would give 2^n complete alternative worlds and n(n-1)/2 bridges between them, and the business names its readings rather than crossing them. A node writes op@<reading> only where the readings genuinely differ; everything else stays single-sourced.

bridges.description: Which pairs of readings produce adjusting entries. Required once more than two readings are declared: past two, 'the difference' is no longer a single thing, and an undeclared bridge is a deliverable nobody agreed to produce. One pair, one bridge.

entry_noun.description: what a decided difference is called here

posted_noun.description: what the total of the ones that land is called

carried_noun.description: what a difference something upstream caused is called

slots.description: The places an entry crossing this bridge must fill. Accounting declares two; another domain declares as many as it has.

checks.description: Articulation assertions — the unit tier. Pure computation over node values, run on every compile. There is no separate reconciliation script by design: if a check ran against anything else, the two could disagree.

at.description: Scoped by the key's presence, not its value: `{期间: null}` means 'only when no period is selected', which is a real scope and not the absence of one.

basis.description: Run this check only under one reading. An assertion that holds under the book figures and not under the restated ones is still worth making.

translations.description: Display-only translations keyed by original text. IDs, formulas and source data remain stable. Declared locales must cover node labels and descriptions.

id.description: The property that names one row. A type that is a view over a table may leave it out and take its backing's key instead — which is the honest answer for a table whose rows need two columns to tell apart, and avoids saying the same thing twice.

dimensions.description: Dimension name -> the property of this type that carries it. A type that declares none is reference data (people, suppliers) and is never filtered out, because dropping it would break every row pointing at it.

from.description: The raw whose dsn this table lives in.

key.description: Columns that identify one row. Checked for uniqueness against the live data, not assumed.

where.description: Which rows of the table belong to this object at all.

backing.description: This type is a view over a table rather than a carrier of rows. Two types may bind the same table: one table often holds more than one business object.

display.description: Property whose value labels a record; identity remains the checked key.

owner.description: Hard rule: never both. Ops may only write owner=ontology.

from.description: Which raw supplies this property. A list means the figure is corroborated: each source writes it as `<prop>@<raw>` on the row, and the compiler decides what their agreement is worth.

to.description: What a ref points at: a declared type name, or 'hook'. A ref to a type is a link — the edge one object follows to another, which is most of what an audit is. A ref to a hook is a gap.

absent.description: What a null means. For a nullable number: 'gap' = not recorded yet (chase it), 'zero' = determined to be none (a finding). For a nullable link: 'gap' = not matched yet, 'none' = determined to have no counterpart. Required, because the two are indistinguishable in the data and opposite in the business.

corroboration.description: Only with a list-valued `from`. A disagreement fails unless the row cites a hook AND `prefer` says which source governs — a preference alone would bury every future disagreement behind it.

at_least.description: How many of the declared sources must actually have spoken.

prefer.description: Which source governs when they disagree. Never sufficient on its own.

op.description: This column is computed, not stored. The same restricted SQL the nodes use, evaluated once per row: bare names are the row's own columns or a node, and `this` is the row's id, so `select sum(x) from T where ref = this` aggregates the rows linked to it. A property with an op must not also be written out per row, and must not declare 'owner' — a formula is a decision of ours, so it is owned here by construction.

scale.description: Decimal places a money column is kept in; default 0. Computed money is rounded half-up to it, so a division cannot leave fifteen decimals in a figure nobody would write.

column.description: The upstream column behind this property, when the names differ. Defaults to the property's own name.

gap.description: The hook that accounts for every absence of this column. Rows read from a source table carry no gap reference of ours — we do not own that table — so the column says it once instead of each row saying it.

prop.description: A source property names the raw it comes from — but a type that is a view over a table names it once on the backing instead, and that is not visible from here, so the rule is enforced by check() rather than restated weakly in this schema.

connector.description: One executable command. Values never enter the spec; they are fetched at render time.

dsn.description: A database the types read through, e.g. sqlite:///<path relative to this spec>. A raw is either a command that fetches (connector) or a database that backs tables (dsn).

blocked_on.description: Which raw the gap sits behind.

resolve_when.description: Abstract until this holds; then it lands as a raw or derived node.

op.description: A restricted SQL subset, parsed by the compiler and never eval'd: `select sum(<prop>) from <Type> [where <cond>]`, `select count(*) from <Type>`, arithmetic over bare node names, and nested aggregates as parenthesised scalar subqueries. No joins, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, DISTINCT, CASE, or other functions.

plug_against.description: This node is a balancing figure; name the independent measure it should agree with.

residual_to.description: Where the divergence from plug_against is registered. A plug with nowhere to put its difference absorbs it silently.

because.description: Names the raw or hook that authorises this node's divergence. Required for every reading the node computes differently under; write because@<reading> per reading, or a bare `because` when every reading shares one — which is what the common two-reading case means.

posts.description: Where the difference lands, keyed by the slots the bridge declares. Omit `entry` entirely to say it lands nowhere.

entry.description: Where the derived difference lands. The slot names are the bridge's, not the framework's; a partly filled entry is refused against the bridge's declared slots.

^(op|because|entry)@.+.description: This node's expression, reason, or posting under one declared reading. Overrides the bare key for that reading alone.

class.description: Reversibility tier: who is allowed to land the write.

writes.description: Every entry must be an owner=ontology property.
